summary: AELIANA is a Godot 4.7.2 Mars simulation for the NASA Space Apps Challenge that teaches aerospace systems engineering through play. Players first balance budget, launch mass, power and science payload in a pre-flight Engineering Bay, then live with those choices on a 196-sector Martian terrain. There they survey 44 mineral deposits, use spectrometry and ground-penetrating radar, craft scanner upgrades from local minerals, and investigate a lava tube. The standout discovery is a flint artifact with signs of deliberate toolmaking, worth +150 science points. A final debrief grades the player on cost, mass margin, power health and science return. The project is aimed at K-12 and university STEM learners, with a roadmap toward a lava tube base, a pressurized rover and multi-crew co-op play.
details: AELIANA: Mars Mission Architecture & Surface Exploration Simulation is an interactive Mars science and engineering game built in Godot 4.7.2 (Forward+ pipeline) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It plays in two phases. In Phase 1, the Engineering Bay, the player makes real aerospace trade-offs before launch. These cover the $450M-$1.2B budget, launch vehicle mass margins (Falcon Heavy, SLS Block 1, Vulcan Centaur), power (MMRTG vs solar) and the science payload (GPR vs Raman spectrometer). In Phase 2 those choices decide how the player survives and performs on a streaming voxel terrain of 196 sectors (Terrain3D). The player surveys 44 mineral deposits, runs spectrometry, traces subsurface voids toward a lava tube, and can fabricate scanner upgrades in the field from local minerals.
